In CNft.sol, the safeTransferFrom function does not execute according to the EIP-1155 specification for success or failure, but instead unconditionally reverts and requires the use of safeBatchTransferFrom. This undermines standard behavior and weakens composability with other protocols.

The function implements an incorrect input validation requiring the index to be greater than 0, making the token at index 0 inaccessible. This violates the ERC721 specification which expects zero-based indexing.

An attacker can use a flashloan and the quitLock function to achieve a large amount of votes for one transaction. It can, depends on the implementation of the modules that will use this contract, be used to pass malicious proposals or exploit any feature that depends on the voting balance.

The cancel function uses a strict "greater than" check ($>$) for the proposal threshold, whereas the propose function allows equality ($\ge$), enabling anyone to cancel a proposal if the proposer's voting power exactly equals the threshold.

The updateBucketExchangeRatesAndClaim function is vulnerable to MEV frontrunning, allowing bots to consistently capture update rewards.
This results in unfair reward distribution and discourages honest users from maintaining bucket states.
